reason: The sources provide enough factual claims regarding Comet West to support a short video script.
story: In 1976, Comet West tore through the inner solar system, putting on a show so blindingly bright that astronomers could study it in broad daylight. Discovered photographically by Richard M. West in August 1975, the magnificent sungrazer plummeted within thirty million kilometers of the Sun by late February 1976. Fueled by intense solar heating and forward scattering, its peak apparent magnitude surged to minus three, rivaling Venus. But the drama was only beginning. As the shattered wanderer swung back out toward the deep cosmos, its nucleus fractured into four distinct pieces under brutal tidal forces. Observers watched in amazement as these glowing fragments drifted apart, leaving behind a massive dust tail spanning up to thirty-five degrees. With an estimated orbital period of hundreds of thousands of years, this cosmic apparition vanished back into the outer solar system, remaining over fifty astronomical units away since 2003.
angle: Comet West was so blindingly bright during its 1976 perihelion passage that astronomers were able to study it in broad daylight.

claims.claim: Comet West was discovered photographically on August 10, 1975.
Richard M. West discovered the comet at the European Southern Observatory.
The comet reached its perihelion on February 25, 1976.
Comet West reached a peak apparent magnitude of minus 3.
Observers reported that the comet was bright enough to study during full daylight from February 25 to 27.
The comet's nucleus was observed to split into four fragments.
The comet has an estimated orbital period varying from 254,000 to 558,000 years.
The comet has been more than 50 AU from the Sun since 2003.
Emission lines of C2, CN, C3, CH, and NH2 were detected from the comet.
Dust particles emitted from its coma contained magnesium-rich silicates and amorphous carbon.
The comet passed within 30 million km of the Sun.
The New York Times reported on March 2, 1976, that the comet was expected to reach maximum visibility in the eastern sky.

disputed: Estimates of the exact orbital period vary between 254,000 and 558,000 years due to perturbations during the splitting event; scripts should attribute the range to varying scientific estimates.
